mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises by >0.5pp in a month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue growth prospects diminish, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production growth exceeding 0.5% monthly, the manufacturing sector's expansion signals robust corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% monthly, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals the start of a monetary tightening cycle, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% in a month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 100,000 per month indicates strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000, or the Rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above 100 indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is above 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a housing market recovery (HOUST > 900 thousand units) and strong retail sales (RSAFS > 420,000 million dollars), consumer spending growth accelerates, boosting corporate revenue and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: housing market recovery and strong retail sales
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 900 and RSAFS > 420000, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.
